documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Abans Finance PLC (AFSL) is a licensed finance company (NBFI) -- single entity, no Group/Company split (the filing presents one set of statements only). Cross-checked shares_in_issue: NAVPS Rs.58.26 = Total Shareholders' Funds 4,293,656,717 / 73,693,171 shares (sum of 20 largest holders 72,737,459 + Others 955,712 = 73,693,171, per note (l)) = 58.26, ties exactly; EPS 138,346,298/73,693,171 = 1.877 rounds to disclosed 1.88. No column-swap issues found. revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (1,015,327,719), the filing's own subtotal = Net Interest Income (918,648,972) + Net Fee & Commission Income (85,888,362) + Net Gain/(Loss) from Trading (3,494,527) + Other Operating Income net (7,295,858). operating_profit = 'Operating Profit before Taxes on Financial Services' (356,364,360), the company's own pre-VATFS subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK even though Interest Income (1,358,495,460) and Interest Expense (439,846,488) are disclosed as separate gross lines -- because the filing nets them to an explicit 'Net Interest Income' subtotal before rolling into Total Operating Income (same structure as this session's CDB/AAF entries), so populating finance_costs/finance_income separately would double count against revenue. tax_expense = 'Income Tax Expense' (114,037,959) only; 'Taxes on Financial Services' (103,980,103) is a separate VAT-on-Financial-Services-type levy sitting between operating_profit and profit_before_tax, consistent with the CDB/AAF/LOFC treatment this session. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split, and 'Loans and Advances' / 'Lease Rentals Receivable & Stock Out on Hire' are the core lending book, not trade receivables. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to Banks' (535,945,533, a small facility consistent with an overdraft-type short-term bank line). long_term_borrowings = 'Other Borrowed Funds' (3,821,274,841), which includes the Rs.1,338,400,000 senior unsecured redeemable debentures issued 30 April 2026 (5-year tenor per note (d)) plus other longer-dated borrowed funds. 'Due to Customers' (12,524,842,905, deposits) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt, per project convention. cash_and_equivalents = Balance Sheet 'Cash and Bank Balances' (1,071,966,043); note the Cash Flow Statement uses a broader definition (period-end cash and cash equivalents of 1,942,613,377, which appears to include short-term placements) -- the narrower BS line is used for consistency with other entries this session. capex = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant and Equipment' (74,204,681) + 'Acquisition of Intangible Assets' (678,895) = 74,883,576. Credit Loss Expense on Financial Assets rose from Rs.99,158,392 (Q1 FY25/26) to Rs.149,382,713 (Q1 FY26/27), +51%, the single largest drag on profit growth this quarter -- flagged as a genuine NPL/impairment driver per instruction. Personnel Costs also rose sharply (+47%, Rs.207.0mn to Rs.303.9mn) and Taxes on Financial Services rose 30% (Rs.80.3mn to Rs.104.0mn), together compressing PBT growth to only 5% despite Net Interest Income growing 37% and Total Operating Income growing 32%. Figures are provisional and subject to audit per the filing's own caveat.

interim_updates.note_text: Abans Finance's Total Operating Income grew 32% YoY to Rs.1,015.3mn in Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), but Profit Before Tax grew only 5% to Rs.252.4mn and PAT 5% to Rs.138.3mn (EPS Rs.1.88 vs Rs.1.79) -- a sharp margin squeeze (operating margin 35.1% vs 41.6%; net margin 13.6% vs 17.1%). The growth engine was Leasing: Leasing interest income rose 42% to Rs.1,199.2mn and the Leasing book expanded 46% YoY to Rs.15.69bn (from Rs.10.71bn), while the small Term Loans book more than doubled (segment assets +129% to Rs.2.89bn, interest income +136% to Rs.106.9mn). Net Interest Income rose 37% to Rs.918.6mn, but every cost line grew faster than that: Interest Expense +79% to Rs.439.8mn (funding the book expansion, including the Rs.1,338.4mn senior unsecured debenture issued 30 April 2026 at 12.50% fixed / AWPLR+2.00% floating, which lifted 'Other Borrowed Funds' 48% to Rs.3.82bn), Credit Loss Expense +51% to Rs.149.4mn (Leasing impairment alone +84% to Rs.115.3mn), Personnel Costs +47% to Rs.303.9mn, Depreciation & Amortisation +74% to Rs.36.5mn and Other Operating Expenses +39% to Rs.169.1mn. Operating profit before levies still rose 11% to Rs.356.4mn, but Taxes on Financial Services jumped 30% to Rs.104.0mn, trimming PBT growth to 5%. Net Fee & Commission Income was flat (+2%) because fee expense more than doubled. Cash flow shows the cost of growth: operating cash flow was -Rs.239.0mn (vs +Rs.316.4mn a year ago) as lease receivables grew Rs.1.19bn and loans Rs.639mn, funded by customer deposits (+Rs.1.49bn; Due to Customers +13% to Rs.12.52bn) and the debenture. Balance sheet: total assets +13% in the quarter to Rs.23.6bn, NAV/share Rs.58.26 (vs Rs.56.39 at March 2026) after an interim dividend of Rs.2.72/share (Rs.200.4mn) paid 21 May 2026. Related-party note: Rs.303.1mn of motorcycles for finance leases were bought from affiliate Abans Auto, 7.15% of total loan disbursements (parent Abans PLC holds 50.22%). Credit rating A-(lka)/Stable (Fitch).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no predecessor quarter is stored for AFSL (this is the first financial_statements entry for the symbol). Comparatives are the filing's own Q1 FY2025/26 column. The Statement of Profit or Loss is provisional and subject to audit (per the filing).
interim_updates.takeaway: Volume growth is strong (leasing book +46%, revenue +32%) but profit is barely growing (+5%) because funding costs, impairments, staff costs and depreciation all rose faster than income -- the company is buying growth at a visibly lower margin, and funding it with costlier wholesale debt (the new debenture) and negative operating cash flow. The quality of the new Leasing book (impairment +84%) is the thing to watch.

operational_highlights: Total Operating Income +32% to Rs.1,015.3mn, but PBT only +5% to Rs.252.4mn and PAT +5% to Rs.138.3mn; operating margin fell to 35.1% from 41.6%
Leasing book +46% YoY to Rs.15.69bn (interest income +42% to Rs.1,199.2mn); Term Loans book +129% to Rs.2.89bn (interest income +136% to Rs.106.9mn)

Interest Expense +79% to Rs.439.8mn outpaced Net Interest Income growth of +37% (Rs.918.6mn) as the Rs.1,338.4mn debenture (12.50% fixed / AWPLR+2.00% floating, issued 30 April 2026) lifted Other Borrowed Funds 48% to Rs.3.82bn
Credit Loss Expense +51% to Rs.149.4mn, with Leasing impairment +84% to Rs.115.3mn -- the main asset-quality flag on the rapidly growing leasing book
Operating cash flow -Rs.239.0mn (vs +Rs.316.4mn a year earlier) as lease receivables rose Rs.1.19bn; funded by Rs.1.49bn of new customer deposits and the debenture
Interim dividend of Rs.2.72/share (Rs.200.4mn) paid 21 May 2026; NAV/share Rs.58.26 (Rs.56.39 at 31 March 2026); Fitch A-(lka)/Stable
key_drivers: Cost growth outran income: Interest Expense +79%, Personnel +47%, D&A +74%, Credit Loss +51% versus Total Operating Income +32% -- the entire reason PBT grew only 5%
Leasing is the growth and risk engine: segment interest income +42%, segment assets +46% to Rs.15.69bn, but segment impairment +84% to Rs.115.3mn
Taxes on Financial Services +30% to Rs.104.0mn widened the gap between pre-levy operating profit growth (+11%) and PBT growth (+5%)
Rs.1,338.4mn debenture (30 April 2026) added costly wholesale funding; 90% (Rs.1.2bn) deployed into the lending book by 30 June, the remaining 10% parked in fixed deposits
